recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add a literal statement that all workflow states live on Task because it would conflict with the current Request/Event pattern model and later status guidance. Future changes should come from a current workflow issue if the work group wants stronger conformance rules around duplicated state across Task, request resources, and event resources.
issue_request: FHIR-5178 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 ballot comment asking for clearer rules on when a stateful healthcare concept should be modeled as a separate resource versus as a lifecycle/status value on an existing resource. The recorded resolution said that, in STU3, workflow states would live on Task rather than Order/Request resources.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed source commit for FHIR-5178 was found. The STU3-era workflow work appears to have been applied through broader workflow-pattern commits, especially git commit 5064224bd079b7f4ef4023d3ead9111b57bd8bff, which aligned resources with Request/Event/Definition patterns and updated the Workflow module without naming this Jira key.
additional_context: The current build includes the Workflow module, Request pattern, and Task resource sources through active source/fhir.ini entries. Current source no longer supports the literal 2015 shorthand that every workflow state belongs only on Task: Request and Event resources have status/intent or status semantics for their own domain lifecycle, while Task is the workflow-management record for assignment, ownership, progress, and fulfillment. Related Jira discussion in FHIR-5707 supports this more nuanced model by recognizing that request and event resources can have separate lifecycle states when workflow boundaries are clear. Zulip and Confluence searches found no direct FHIR-5178 community record or conflicting later work-group decision.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source hunk was needed because the active Workflow module distinguishes Request, Event, and Workflow Management; the Request pattern delegates fulfillment/execution to Task; and Task narrative explains its execution, assignment, progress, and fulfillment role.

related_jiras.note: Related ProcedureRequest/Procedure status discussion supports the current nuanced model where request and event resources can each have lifecycle status, provided workflow boundaries are clear.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 ballot comment asking for clearer rules about lifecycle status values versus separate workflow resources, resolved by pointing workflow states toward Task for STU3.
evidence_items.learned: This final issue establishes the need to audit current workflow/status boundary guidance rather than make a resource-specific status change.

evidence_items.summary: Active build configuration lists workflow-module, the Request pattern, and task=Task.
evidence_items.learned: The inspected Workflow, Request, and Task source files are part of the current build surface.

evidence_items.summary: The Workflow module describes Request/Event patterns and says Task manages task-level assignment, ownership, progress, and fulfillment state.
evidence_items.learned: Current source gives implementers the requested boundary guidance in the modern Request/Event/Task model.

evidence_items.summary: The Request pattern says intent distinguishes proposal/plan/order and status records request lifecycle, while Task handles assignment, progress, and fulfillment.
evidence_items.learned: Request resources intentionally retain request lifecycle state, so no literal Task-only rewrite is appropriate.

evidence_items.summary: Task tracks execution, assignment, progress, and fulfillment without changing the meaning of referenced request or event resources.
evidence_items.learned: Task has the workflow-management role needed to satisfy the seed's concern without displacing all domain status values.

evidence_items.summary: 2017 commit 'Applied workflow-related tracker items' aligned resources with workflow patterns and updated Workflow/Request sources without naming FHIR-5178.
evidence_items.learned: The historical application appears to be broad workflow-pattern work rather than an explicit seed-keyed commit.

evidence_items.summary: Related Published ProcedureRequest/Procedure status discussion recorded that both request and event status concepts are appropriate when workflow boundaries are clarified.
evidence_items.learned: This supports preserving the current nuanced Request/Event/Task guidance instead of enforcing a literal all-states-on-Task rule.
